newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seguin says French Giscard EMU views "impeccable".
newsitem.headline: Seguin says French Giscard EMU views "impeccable".

text.p: Gaullist National Assemby speaker and former anti-Maastricht campaigner Philippe Seguin said on Thursday that ex-President Valery Giscard d'Estaing's remarks on European monetary union were "impeccable" and made "good sense".

"Valery Giscard d'Estaing has put the debate on Europe back on the correct footing. The problems is no longer about whether we are going to have a single currency, but how we go about it. We cannot steer around that," Seguin told reporters.

"Valery Giscard d'Estaing has hit the nail on the head by stating that employment is the absolute priority, evoking the crucial issue of the relationship between the euro and the dollar and indirectly the franc-mark relationship," he said.
"The way forward has been mapped out," Seguin added.

Giscard d'Estaing said in an article published in weekly magazine l'Express on Wednesday that France should announce plans to fix the franc against the euro at a much lower level than it is now, opening to way to a depreciation which would revive growth.

He argued that the government should announce that the franc would be fixed at seven francs per euro -- corresponding to a more appropriate level against the dollar of 5.49 francs per dollar, compared to 5.08 francs currently.
This would correspond to a level of 3.65 francs per mark still within the 15 percent fluctuation bands permitted under the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), he said.

The government should announce its target exchange rate for the franc against the euro in the next few days or in any case before the end of the year to set the French currency on course towards this rate and avoid instability in the switch to the single currency in 1999, he said.
The best time, he suggested, would be just after parliament approved its deficit-cutting 1997 budget. The National Assembly, the lower house of parliament, approved the budget on Wednesday.

Giscard said he had always believed the most important decision for France ahead of EMU was to decide the rate at which the franc would be fixed irrevocably against the euro since Paris would, from 1999, never again have the option to adjust its exchange rate to boost growth.
The franc, however, was currently overvalued against the dollar and this was the main reason for weak growth and "intolerable" levels of unemployment, he said.

The overvaluation was due to a "stubborn" determination to keep the franc level-pegging with the mark, despite a sharp rise in the German currency due to the high German interest rates imposed after unification.
The franc should be brought back to the rate against the dollar seen at the start of the 1990s, in other words at 5.50 francs. -- Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 frs/bfl
